bib.title: Can LLMs Convert Graphs to Text-Attributed Graphs?

read.skipped: References skimmed; case-study text in Appendix F skimmed.

question: Can an LLM convert graphs with little or no node text into text-attributed graphs so one GNN can be trained across graphs with different feature spaces?
hypothesis: Feeding topological properties and neighbour text into an LLM yields node descriptions that explain a node's role and give better, more transferable features than manual topology features or existing LLM augmentation (TAPE, KEA).
contributions: First method (TANS) to use LLMs to generate node descriptions for graphs of any text availability (text-rich, text-limit, text-free)
Prompt that injects five computed topological properties with ranks plus optional node and neighbour text
Experiments on single-graph learning, domain adaptation and pretrain-finetune

method.summary: For each node, compute five topological properties, build a templated prompt (graph/node type, optional node text, 5 random neighbour texts, property values and percentile ranks), ask GPT-4o-mini for the top-k likely classes with reasons (under 200 words), then embed the output (appended to original text where it exists) with a small text encoder and train a GCN/GAT/MLP on the embeddings.
method.task: node classification with feature alignment across graphs

prompts.text: Given a node from a {Graph Type} graph, where the node type is {Node Type} with {Node Number} nodes, and the edge type is {Edge Type} with {Edge Number} edges.
The original node description is {Original Textual Descriptions}.
The following are the textual information of {k} connected nodes. The descriptions are: {Textual Descriptions of Selected Neighborhoods}.
The value of {Node Property} is {Value of The Given Property}, ranked as {Rank of The Node}% among {Node Number} nodes.
Output the potential {k} classes of the node and provide reasons for your assessment. The classes include {Classes of Nodes}. Your answer should be less than 200 words.

limits: No graphs above 100,000 nodes: querying GPT per node is costly; ogbn-products is a 54,000-node subsample
Only GPT-4o-mini tried; authors say unclear whether GPT-4o would do better
Prompt-design ablations limited by cost; only neighbour text and topology removal tested
Only node classification; edge and graph tasks left to future work
Gains over TAPE/KEA on text-rich graphs are small (about 1 to 1.5 points average) relative to std of 1.5 to 2; no significance test
Hyperparameters tuned per method with 500 Bayesian runs, but best test-reported performance is selected; tuning budget for baselines not detailed
Airport tasks are small (131 to 1,190 nodes) with large std (Brazil up to 17 points)
Negative transfer observed in some cases and declared out of scope
No LLM-cost or latency figures given; possible LLM pretraining contamination on Cora/Pubmed not discussed
Decoding settings (temperature) and generation date of GPT-4o-mini not stated
